headline: Historic Old Town and Marine Reserve Reservations
reservation: Access to Dry Tortugas National Park requires ferry or seaplane bookings months in advance; this is distinct from local reef charters or state park entry. State parks like Fort Zachary Taylor and Bahia Honda use day-use fees, while specialized marine excursions have limited capacity. Verify all systems via official NPS and Florida State Parks portals.

days.title: Old Town Immersion and Sunset Waterfront
days.start: Suggested: 2 PM from Key West International Airport (EYW)

stops.name: Duval Street Historic District
stops.detail: Walk the primary cultural artery to observe preserved Victorian architecture and local galleries.

stops.name: Mallory Square
stops.detail: Join the community gathering for the sunset view, a traditional first-evening transition to island time.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; island traffic and pedestrian zones vary
days.note: Most Old Town attractions are manageable on foot; bicycles are a local alternative.

days.title: Coastal Heritage and Coral Reefs
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Historic Seaport

stops.name: Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
stops.detail: Depart via licensed charter to snorkel the only living coral barrier reef in the continental United States.

stops.name: Fort Zachary Taylor Historic State Park
stops.detail: Explore the Civil War-era masonry fort before visiting the park's specific rocky beach zone.

days.driving: Walking or local transfer suggested; parking is highly limited
days.note: Marine visibility and boat departures depend entirely on wind and sea states.

days.title: Lower Keys Ecology and Overseas Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Old Town Key West

stops.name: Bahia Honda State Park
stops.detail: View the historic Over-the-Sea Railway bridge and access the park's natural sandy shorelines.

stops.name: National Key Deer Refuge
stops.detail: Observe the endangered subspecies from official viewing areas on Big Pine Key; never feed wildlife.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours round trip; conditions on the Overseas Highway vary
days.note: Drive cautiously through Big Pine Key to protect active wildlife crossings.

intel.title: Old Town Constraints
intel.text: Parking in the historic district is strictly regulated with limited residential permits and paid lots. Confirm if your lodging provides off-street spots before arrival.

intel.title: Marine Sanctuary Rules
intel.text: Use reef-safe sun protection and never touch coral formations within the sanctuary. Specific snorkeling zones may be closed for restoration or weather.

intel.title: Overseas Highway Service
intel.text: Fuel is available at major keys like Big Pine and Marathon, but stations are spaced out. Check levels before starting a Lower Keys loop.

intel.title: Dry Tortugas Departure
intel.text: Ferry check-ins typically begin very early at the terminal. Missing the strict departure window will result in a forfeited reservation.

intel.title: Remote Keys Coverage
intel.text: Expect intermittent cellular service in the remote parts of the Key Deer Refuge and on the open water. Download offline maps for Lower Keys navigation.

plan.arrival: Collect bags at EYW, secure a taxi or rental, and drop luggage at your Old Town base before exploring the compact historic core.
plan.vehicle: A car is essential for the Lower Keys, but a liability in Old Town; check for narrow-street rental restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Mallory Square is the traditional sunset choice, but Fort Zachary Taylor offers a more natural shoreline perspective.
